The proof of Proposition 4.2 given above essentially repeats the classical proof of the fact that the stack $\underline{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mu}$ defined in §4.2.1 is a scheme of finite type (affine over $C^{\mu}$ ) in a “relative” setting over $\mathrm{Bun}_{T}$ . Alternatively, these properties can be deduced from the latter facts using Proposition 4.8 below.

4.2. Some fibers

We continue with our $\mu\in\mathbf{Y}_{\succeq 0}$ . In this subsection we introduce two slightly different schemes obtained from $\mathbf{Z}^{\mu}$ that appear in many references. See Remark 4.10 below for a relation between these two schemes.

4.2.1. The “classical” Zastava scheme

We set

$\underline{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mu}:=\{\mathcal{F}^{0}\}\times_{\mathrm{Bun}_{T},p_{1}}\mathbf{Z}^{\mu}.$

By Proposition 4.2, $\underline{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mu}$ is
a scheme of finite type over $\mathbb{F}$ . It is equipped with a canonical morphism
$\underline{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mu}\to C^{\mu}$ , which is affine.
Concretely, this scheme classifies the following data:

•

a point $E$ of $C^{\mu}(S)$ ;

•

a $G$ -torsor $\mathcal{E}$ on $C\times S$ ;

•

a trivialization $\beta$ of $\mathcal{E}_{|(C\times S)\smallsetminus E}$

paper.title: Modular intersection cohomology of Drinfeld's compactifications
paper.abstract: We compute the dimension of the cohomology of stalks of intersection cohomology complexes on Zastava schemes and Drinfeld compactifications associated with a connected reductive algebraic group $G$, in case the characteristic of the coefficients field $\Bbbk$ is good for $G$. In particular, we show that these dimensions do not depend on the choice of $\Bbbk$.
